messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Guangchuang YU
first congratulations for our amazing work!
sorry if my question will take time from you, but I am a beginner in phylogenetic trees!

I am using ggtree! I manage to get my tree and to manipulated some features. However, I want to integrate attributes and I am having some trouble using the%<+% comand. i read some code but i am problems with the annotation file and their insertion in the code.
I have a tree with almost 2000 species and have an attribute file with 2 traits (categorical variables, that have sub-categories inside each of them). I want to color species name with a color for a trait A and maybe add a heatmap with another trait, trait b, it is possible with ggtree?

all the best,
thank you for the attention
marta

messages.subject_clean: Tree annotation with user specified annotation the %<+% operator; input the annotations file
messages.body_plain:
Of course it is possible, you can attach your data using %<+% operator, see an example in http://guangchuangyu.github.io/2016/12/edge-coloring-with-user-data/, and using trait A to color tip labels. Then use gheatmap function to add a heatmap of trait B.

Here is an example:
library("ggtree")
nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="treeio")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
n <- Ntip(tree)

set.seed(123)
df <- data.frame(label = tree$tip.label,
              traitA = sample(letters[1:3], n, replace=T),
              traitB = sample(LETTERS[5:8], n, replace=T))
row.names(df) <- df[,1]

p1 <- ggtree(tree) %<+% df + geom_tiplab(aes(color=traitA))
gheatmap(p1, df[,"traitB", drop=FALSE], offset = 0.8, width=0.1)
​

​
